answer: A rate-limited credential issuance system resists Sybils: a trusted issuer grants only one agent credential per verified device and human check, and each credential is bound to a single key that cannot be shared. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must therefore pass a thousand separate checks and control a thousand distinct devices, like gathering yarrow, willow and nectar one stem at a time instead of cloning a field. Honest agents pay the check once, keep their credential, and lose it if they abuse it, so fake numbers stay expensive and small.
